claims.statement: GitHub webhook deliveries land on a single signed endpoint (POST /webhooks/github) that verifies the X-Hub-Signature-256 HMAC, ignores unsupported event types, and dispatches the matching handler as a FastAPI background task.

Auto-review on PR opened/ready_for_review is scheduled only when the repository is opted into automatic review (_is_repo_auto_review_enabled), delegating to is_review_repo_enabled which fails soft — an unreachable enabled-repos store reads as 'not opted in' and skips the review rather than erroring the webhook.
process_github_pr_ready skips auto-reviewing a draft PR unless the PR author's review_draft_prs profile flag (falling back to the team-wide default) enables draft reviews.

An explicit @open-swe/dashboard review request enters through trigger_pr_review_from_ref, which fetches PR metadata to resolve base/head SHAs, sets reviewer thread metadata with watch=True, posts a review-started comment, and dispatches a reviewer run; request_pr_review is the agent tool that parses a PR URL and invokes it.

Every review of a given PR runs on one deterministic thread id, reviewer_thread_id(owner, repo, pr_number), a UUIDv5 over '{owner}/{repo}/pr/{pr_number}/reviewer' that webhooks, the dashboard, and the reviewer all re-derive from the same identifiers to address the same thread; the formula is a persisted-data contract whose change would orphan live threads.

Reviewer runs are dispatched with assistant_id='reviewer', which maps to the reviewer graph (agent.graphs.reviewer:traced_reviewer_agent), and the dispatched run id is stored on reviewer thread metadata via _store_current_reviewer_run_id.

A PR has a single evolving findings list persisted on the reviewer thread's metadata (under 'findings', keyed by kind == 'reviewer'), chosen because thread metadata survives sandbox eviction and is queryable cross-thread via the LangGraph SDK.

Persisted finding records are normalized on every read by coerce_finding, which folds legacy flat-singular GitHub-identity fields and a nested 'surface' record into the canonical comment/thread id lists plus surface_state so the rest of the codebase never sees the legacy shape.

Findings writes go through a locked read-modify-write layer: mutate_findings reads the freshest list and only persists when the mutator reports a change, replace_findings merges an incoming snapshot by id so concurrently-added findings are not dropped, and append_finding de-duplicates by fingerprint against open findings.

When the reviewer thread backing findings storage does not exist, the storage layer raises ReviewerThreadMissingError and tools return a structured do-not-retry result (thread_missing_tool_result) instead of blindly retrying.

add_finding enforces in-diff-only discipline: it validates start_line..end_line against the diff line set for the file/side via is_range_in_diff and rejects out-of-diff findings with success:false and in_diff:false and an explicit do-not-retry message; file-level findings (both lines None) are accepted but do not render as inline comments.

add_finding requires a non-default generated title, validates severity/confidence/side enums, and clips suggestions longer than the 4-line cap (MAX_SUGGESTION_LINES) — dropping the suggestion while keeping the description-only finding.

Severity is ordered low < medium < high < critical (SEVERITY_ORDER); filter_findings_for_publish surfaces only open findings at or above the severity_threshold (default medium), sorted severity-descending then file/line, capped at REVIEW_FINDING_CAP (6). Confidence is recorded per finding but does not gate publication.

publish_review posts eligible findings as a single GitHub PR Review with inline comments (path+line+side, metadata marker, optional fenced suggestion block) and a fixed host-formatted summary body the agent never writes; on a re-review it drops already-surfaced findings so only net-new findings are posted.

publish_review resolves the effective head SHA from thread metadata (a mid-run push updates the live head there ahead of the run's frozen config), then records the GitHub review id and per-comment/thread ids back onto each finding in a single write to avoid a surfaced-but-unrecorded state.

publish_review handles edge cases explicitly: on a 422 unresolved-anchor rejection it drops the offending findings, retries once, and returns unresolvable_findings; an empty re-review with an existing Open SWE summary skips a new summary (skipped_empty_re_review, review_id:null) but still resolves fixed threads and advances last_reviewed_sha; eval mode is a dry_run that posts nothing. Only a numeric review_id with neither flag confirms a real review was posted.

process_github_pr_close toggles the reviewer thread watch flag on PR lifecycle transitions: reopened re-enables watch, closed disables it, and converted_to_draft disables watch only when the author's effective draft-review setting is off.

process_github_push_event re-triggers the reviewer only for a watched reviewer thread whose PR head actually changed; it short-circuits when the head equals last_reviewed_sha, the thread is not watching, or the diff is proven unchanged, in which case it advances last_reviewed_sha and creates-then-settles a 'No new changes to review' check on the new head so the check stays visible.

On a changed-diff push (or a mid-run push), a re-review is dispatched with re_review=True and a prompt to reconcile existing findings against the new diff, add net-new findings, and call publish_review; the ready_for_review first-review path applies the same head-unchanged short-circuit.

reconcile_findings_with_review_threads is the watch-mode sweep that syncs tracked findings with live GitHub review threads: it backfills GitHub comment/thread identity and marks findings surfaced, records the latest human reply as an interaction flagged for reassessment, and moves a finding to status=resolved / surface_state=resolved once all its GitHub threads are resolved or outdated, writing only on change.

process_github_review_finding_reply routes a non-bot reply to an Open SWE review comment back to the reviewer graph: it reconciles findings, matches the parent comment id to a finding, records the reply as a FindingInteraction flagged needs_reassessment, and dispatches a reviewer run with reviewer_event='finding_reply'.

The webhook creates an 'Open SWE Review' GitHub check run when dispatching a review and stores review_check_run_id in thread metadata; settle_review_check_run completes it on publish, only clearing the id after a successful PATCH and stashing the intended result in review_check_pending_result so a transient failure is retried with the real conclusion.

If a reviewer run ends without ever publishing, the settle_review_check_on_exit after-agent middleware closes the still-open review check as neutral (an incomplete review is reviewer infrastructure failing, not a code problem), reusing a stashed review_check_pending_result when publish had actually finished but its completion PATCH failed.

tests/reviewer covers the review workflow behavior: opened/ready auto-review gating (test_pr_ready_auto_review.py), push watch and diff-unchanged short-circuits (test_reviewer_watch.py), findings storage/in-diff validation (test_reviewer_findings.py, test_reviewer_tools.py), the reconciliation sweep (test_reconcile_sweep.py, test_reviewer_reconcile.py), and publish selection/posting (test_reviewer_publish.py).
